solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Thrice I'd my pees malfunctioning in tubes 'down there'

indicators.note: something malfunctioning is out of order, so the letters before it are put in a new order

blocks.note: the contraction I'D written out three times
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man complains that something is going wrong with his plumbing when he relieves himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The epididymides are the coiled ducts behind the testes, so the urinary surface is fittingly close to the anatomy; the quoted 'down there' is the coy euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: The epididymides are the coiled sperm ducts at the back of each testicle, tubes in the genital region.

clue.text: Decay enveloping bones with time in stone circle

indicators.note: enveloping means wrapping round, so the word for decay is split to hold the rest

blocks.note: to perish is to rot or decay
tali, plural of talus, are ankle bones
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Archaeologists find a ring of standing stones crumbling, with skeletons buried inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A peristalith is a ring of standing stones surrounding a burial mound, so it is a kind of stone circle.

clue.text: Rev troubled about half of us appearing in area of special Sabbath licence

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed or stirred up, so the letters of the cleric's title are jumbled
half of a two-letter word is just one of its letters, here the leading one
about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the selected one

blocks.note: taken as written; jumbled to ERV
the first of the two letters of us

explanation.surface: A worried vicar wanders around a sacred zone set apart for the Sabbath.
explanation.walkthrough: An eruv is a Jewish ritual boundary within which carrying objects is allowed on the Sabbath, hence the special licence.
explanation.definitionFit: An eruv is an enclosed district in which Jewish law relaxes the Sabbath ban on carrying things outdoors.

clue.text: Dry off to hide maze of blood vessels

indicators.note: off means taken away, so the word for dry is removed from the word for hide

blocks.note: to secrete something is to hide it
sec is French for dry, used of wine; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Instructions to dry something off and conceal it in a labyrinth.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Dry off to hide' as SECRETE with SEC taken off the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A rete is an anatomical network or plexus of blood vessels or nerves, a mesh fairly described as a maze.

clue.text: Swears the government is on limits of trustworthiness

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its two ends, so only its outermost letters are kept

blocks.note: the ins are the party in office, as opposed to the outs
taken as written
first and last letters of trustworthiness

explanation.surface: Someone vows that the government relies on being trustworthy at the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the later pieces beneath the earlier ones.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist is to declare something emphatically, close in sense to swearing that it is so.

clue.text: Came across upcoming opening – when?

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: to come across someone is to meet them; reads TEM going up
a pore is a small opening in the skin

explanation.surface: Someone asks when an imminent launch they heard about is actually happening.
explanation.walkthrough: Tempore is Latin, used in dates as 'in the time of', so a question about time fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempore is the Latin for 'in the time of', marking the period when something happened, hence 'when?'.

clue.text: Divine drink maiden's drained from fine porcelain

indicators.note: something drained from a vessel is taken out of it, so a letter leaves the word

blocks.note: amrita is the drink of immortality of the Hindu gods
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over; removed

explanation.surface: A heavenly drink has been poured out of delicate china.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'has', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Arita is a Japanese porcelain named after the town in Kyushu where it is made.

clue.text: Cal. City guy tops eminent scientist in local tasks

indicators.note: to top something is to cut off its head, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: Los Angeles, the Californian city
bo is American slang for a pal or fellow
a Fellow of the Royal Society; the first letter is cut off

explanation.surface: A man from a Californian city outdoes a famous scientist at some neighbourhood chores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' refers back to Cal., asking for the American spelling without the U.
explanation.definitionFit: Labors is the American spelling of labours, meaning tasks or pieces of work, local to the US city named.

clue.text: Oily punter splashed out very little

indicators.note: splashing sends things flying in all directions, so these letters land in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, then jumbled
tiny means very small

explanation.surface: A greasy gambler spent hardly anything at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Splashed out' suggests spending lavishly, which clashes with 'very little'; here it only signals the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Turpentiny means resembling or smelling of turpentine, an oily resin, so it describes something oily.

clue.text: Hostelry teed off with variegated plant parts

indicators.note: off here means gone bad or awry, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pub set off a golf ball, with assorted bits of greenery on show.
explanation.definitionFit: Heterostyled plants have styles of different lengths in different flowers, so their floral parts vary.

clue.text: Dad maybe with age, 50, not concerned with digestive system

blocks.note: a dad is an example of a parent
an era is an age
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A father in his fifties is unbothered by his stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Parenteral describes drugs or feeding given by a route other than the gut, such as injection, so bypassing digestion.

clue.text: Soapstone that can be bought cold, set with diamonds, tons (10, two words)

indicators.note: a jewel is set into a mount, so the word for purchasable holds the gems inside it

blocks.note: venal means open to bribery, able to be bought
ice is slang for diamonds
T is the abbreviation for tons
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A mineral is sold off cheaply, its setting studded with jewels by the ton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That can be bought' means corruptible, and ice is underworld slang for diamonds; the two-word answer is a trade name for the mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: Venice talc is a name for steatite, the soft soapy mineral also called soapstone.

clue.text: Type of sword, of something not unalike tar abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means left behind, so those letters are dropped from the longer word

blocks.note: simitar is a Chambers spelling of scimitar, a sword not unlike the one defined
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A sword is described as resembling a sailor who has been deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tar' looks like the sailor, but it is just the three letters to drop from SIMITAR, a variant spelling of scimitar, the curved sword like a simi.
explanation.definitionFit: A simi is a short two-edged sword or knife used in East Africa, one kind of sword.

clue.text: Abrasive, displaying bits of rude temper (but only bits)

indicators.note: only bits are kept, meaning just a small piece, the opening letter, of each word

blocks.note: the first letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Someone abrasive shows flashes of a rude temper, though only now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket tells you to take only the opening letters of the four words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bort is low-grade diamond fragments crushed into powder for use as an abrasive in cutting and grinding.

clue.text: Strip from e.g. prawn almost always involved in first half of meal?

indicators.note: almost means not quite, so the last letter of the following word is cut
only the first half of the word for a meal is kept, the rest dropped
something involved in another is wrapped up inside it

blocks.note: dinner is a meal; only its first half is used
ever means always; its last letter is lost

explanation.surface: A cook explains that a prawn is nearly always cleaned at the start of the dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The vein of a prawn is its gut, removed in preparation; the question mark flags the 'e.g.' definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To devein a prawn or shrimp is to remove the dark intestinal vein running along its back.

clue.text: Piece of (Greek) pottery found in excavation (not the first)?

indicators.note: a piece of a word is a small part of it, here its opening letter
something found in a place is inside it, so one piece goes within the other
not the first means the opening letter is removed

blocks.note: a hole is an excavation; its first letter is dropped
the opening letter of pottery

explanation.surface: A shard of ancient Greek pottery turns up in an archaeological dig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of' does double duty: part of the definition and the signal to take one letter of pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: An olpe is an ancient Greek jug with a single handle, a type of pottery vessel.

clue.text: Bone suffers? Take out

indicators.note: out means removed, so the letter standing for take leaves the word

blocks.note: to incur a loss is to suffer it
R is short for recipe, Latin for 'take', on prescriptions; removed

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a bone hurts and is told to take it out.
explanation.walkthrough: The R that heads old prescriptions stands for recipe, Latin for 'take'.
explanation.definitionFit: The incus, or anvil, is the middle one of the three small bones in the ear.

clue.text: Spoils set out? Not much of a stretch in India

definitions.text: Not much of a stretch in India

indicators.note: out means taken away, so the following word is removed from the word for spoils

blocks.note: to cosset is to pamper or spoil
taken as written; removed

explanation.surface: A doting parent spoils the children; laying out the table is hardly much effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoils' looks like loot, but it is the verb for pampering.
explanation.definitionFit: A coss is an Indian measure of distance of a mile or two, a short stretch of road.

clue.text: Treasurer increasingly stingy about what's central to account

indicators.note: what is central to a word is its middle, a single letter here
about means surrounding, so the word for stingier wraps round the letter

blocks.note: harder means more hard, more tight-fisted
the middle letter of account

explanation.surface: A club treasurer grows ever more miserly over the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treasurer' suggests an official, but here it is someone who treasures and stores things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarder treasures up and stockpiles things, so a treasurer in the literal, not official, sense.

clue.text: Flier turning up – not much is revealed

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: a bird is a flier

explanation.surface: A bird appears overhead, but very little of it can be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: A drib is a small amount, as in 'dribs and drabs', so very little.

clue.text: Old surveyor's instrument, base in wobbly tripod

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
something wobbly is unsteady, so its letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: e is the base of natural logarithms
taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: A surveyor's antique device rests its foot on a shaky three-legged stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like the foot of the tripod but is the mathematical constant e.
explanation.definitionFit: A diopter was an ancient optical sighting instrument for measuring angles, used in early surveying.

clue.text: Salt can when overturning in lake

indicators.note: overturning flips a thing, so the word is read backwards
in places the flipped word inside the name of the lake

blocks.note: Lake Erie, one of the North American Great Lakes
a tin is a can; read upwards

explanation.surface: Salt in a container is spilt when it is tipped over into a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Erinite is a copper arsenate mineral, a salt in the chemical sense of an acid combined with a metal.

clue.text: Change label for small bird left in cage of another

indicators.note: a bird in a cage is enclosed, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: a ree is a female ruff, another bird
a tit is a small songbird
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A little bird's tag is changed after it is left in another bird's cage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' means another bird: the ree is the female of the ruff, a wading bird, a word met mostly in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To retitle something is to give it a new name, so to change the label attached to it.

clue.text: Feature of grate, hot, in a barbecue?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: A, then spit, the rod for roasting meat
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Is a hot grill a feature of a barbecue?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grate' and 'barbecue' both evoke cooking over a fire, but the definition is the fireplace grate.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashpit is the space beneath a fire grate where the ashes collect, part of the fireplace.

clue.text: Improves version of indefinable quality in orchestral section

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the reeds are the woodwind section of an orchestra
it is that indefinable something, sex appeal or charisma

explanation.surface: A conductor polishes a new arrangement that gives the woodwinds a certain something.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-edit a text is to work on it again, producing an improved version.

clue.text: Sits out among soldiers? All one needs for meals with them

definitions.text: All one needs for meals with them

indicators.note: out means disordered here, so the letters are rearranged
among means in the midst of, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written, then jumbled
soldiers are men

explanation.surface: Someone sits out among the troops, wondering what is needed to eat with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Them' points back to the soldiers: the definition leans on the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess tin is a soldier's metal dish that serves as plate and cooking pot, the sole kit for army meals.

clue.text: What's a sot drunk – only the first of that?

definitions.text: What's a sot drunk – only the first of that?

indicators.note: something drunk is reeling and unsteady, so the letters lurch into a new order
only the first of a word means keeping its opening letter alone

blocks.note: taken as written, then jumbled
the opening letter of that

explanation.surface: What does a drunkard knock back, and is it just the first glass?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a drink raised in salute is what even a sot might drink, perhaps just as the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A toast is a drink taken in someone's honour, so something a drinker swallows to begin the evening.

clue.text: OT text: short form of it accompanies funeral rites

indicators.note: a short form of a word keeps only one of its letters, here the final one

blocks.note: the last letter of it
obit is an old word for funeral rites

explanation.surface: A note on a Bible passage reads like an obituary attached to a burial service.
explanation.walkthrough: The Book of Tobit is in the Apocrypha, which some Bibles include with the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobit is a book of the Apocrypha placed among the Old Testament books in Catholic Bibles.

clue.text: Girl switching parts in drive?

indicators.note: switching parts means the two halves change places, front going to back

blocks.note: chit is a derogatory word for a girl or young woman; the run of letters inside 'switching' is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A young woman takes turns at the wheel on a car journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' suggests a car journey; here it is an urge, with a question mark for the loose fit.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a restless craving or urge, and a drive is a strong inner impulse to do something.

clue.text: Peter with yen for purchasing living?

blocks.note: the apostle Peter was first called Simon
Y is the abbreviation for yen, the Japanese currency

explanation.walkthrough: A living is a church benefice; simony is named after Simon Magus, who tried to buy spiritual powers.
explanation.definitionFit: Simony is the buying or selling of church offices, such as a parish benefice known as a living.

clue.text: Blend extract of camel dung

indicators.note: an extract is a portion drawn out of something, here a run of letters spanning two words

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A recipe calls for mixing in an essence of camel droppings.
explanation.definitionFit: To meld is to merge or combine things together, the same as to blend them.

clue.text: Old and young one reared in Orcadian estate

indicators.note: something reared is raised up, which in a down entry means reading upwards

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a lad is a young man; read upwards

explanation.walkthrough: Orcadian means from Orkney, the Scottish islands where udal or odal tenure survived.
explanation.definitionFit: Odal, or udal, is land held in absolute ownership under old Norse law, as in Orkney and Shetland.

clue.text: Moisture mark in pump?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

clue.text: Translation from Latin left out – it's not found in formal language

definitions.text: it's not found in formal language

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'it ain't', which means 'it's not' and is avoided in formal writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ain't is a colloquial contraction of 'is not' or 'am not', regarded as nonstandard and kept out of formal use.

clue.text: Liquor is Scotch to put in calendar?

taken as written
till is Scots for 'to'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' wants to be whisky, but it signals a Scots word: till means 'to' in Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: A distillate is the product of distilling, such as spirits, a strong alcoholic liquor.

clue.text: Style traced thus?

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A handwriting expert wonders whether a hand was drawn in a haphazard manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is its own instruction: write the letters of the first two words in a scattered way.
explanation.definitionFit: Scatteredly means in a dispersed, haphazard way, the way the letters of the clue have been spread.
